site_process.notes: Baseline line operating since Aug 2025 (S12): 'up to 14,000 tonnes of battery manufacturing scrap annually' (S11). Full line (cells/modules/packs) mechanically complete, commissioning from early Sept 2026, 'increases annual processing capacity from 14,000 to 20,000 metric tons of battery feedstock'. Status 'commissioning' refers to the expanded line; baseline continues operating. Planned ultimate capacity 'up to 50,000 tons of battery feedstock annually' (S10, planned). Process includes discharge and thermal treatment (Blacksand = 'thermally treated' black mass); no separate rows for those stages because capacities are not stated separately.
Website: process 'safely discharges Li-ion batteries'. Operating as of baseline commissioning (S11).

'30,000 metric tons of shredding capacity'; product page: 'capability to process up to 30,000 metric tons of battery materials through our shredding lines'. Release says shredding lines 'will produce black mass' from scrap and EoL batteries - whether running now not stated.

'2,500-metric-ton lithium carbonate production line, with space allocated for an additional 2,500-metric-ton line'. Route: 'calciner-based crystallization and water-based precipitation' extracting lithium from black mass - includes a thermal (calciner) step, so classification as hydro vs pyro is a judgement call. 'Initiation of operations' 2026-09-10; funds used to upgrade line toward continuous commercial operation, hence 'commissioning'. Produced Li2CO3 in 2025 under Ascend.

DOE round-2 selection (2024-09-20): retrofit to recycle Li-ion battery production scrap into components (CAM per DOE descriptions); 'annual output of 20,000 metric tons per year'. No evidence of award finalisation or construction; Nov 2025 Florence restart release (S7) does not mention Li-ion.

'10,000 tonne per annum LFP CAM recycling and manufacturing plant'; also '5 GWh of LFP CAM annually'. No later news found on Li Industries' site or elsewhere; grant status after 2025 DOE review unknown.
